note: The great sevillanas groups and singers of the Feria and the Rocío first (Los Marismeños, Amigos de Gines, Los Romeros de la Puebla, María del Monte, the Hermanos Toronjo), then Carlos Saura's 1992 film anthology, the corraleras of Lebrija, and the older 78s of the 1920s-1940s. Years are left open where the only page is a later compilation.

size.basis: Sevillanas are an annual industry: the first discs of sevillanas came from the Hermanos Toronjo from 1950, and each group or singer usually releases a disc of sevillanas every year before Seville's April Fair (es.wikipedia, Los Romeros de la Puebla); the most prolific years were the 'boom de las sevillanas' of 1983-1988 (es.wikipedia, Sevillanas). Los Romeros de la Puebla alone list about 55 albums from 1968 to 2011, Los del Río more than 40, El Pali more than 20; dozens of other groups (Amigos de Gines, Los Marismeños, Cantores de Híspalis, Salmarina, Los Choqueros, Ecos del Rocío, the coros rocieros) and solo singers add their own yearly discs of about ten sevillanas each, besides 78s of the 1920s-1940s by copla singers. MusicBrainz holds only 40 releases with sevillanas in the title, so it covers this Spanish regional market thinly and does not bound the count. Range is a reasoned guess, not a catalogue count; core is what an Andalusian listener would call essential (the classic sevillanas of the main groups, the Rocío standards, the 1980s boom hits).
